CONTINUED TAXI ACROSS RAMP AND DOWN RUNWAY 29 WITH NO OTHER INDICATIONS OF AN ISSUE. UPON ROTATING AT 96 KIAS FELT THE LEFT MAIN GEAR “GRAB” AS IF BRAKES HAD BEEN APPLIED. DURING A SCHEDULED INSPECTION IT WAS NOTED THAT THERE WAS EXHAUST GAS STREAKING IN THE ENGINE INLET COMING FROM THE AFT EDGE OF THE STAINLESS STEEL HEATED DEICE LIP.  UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION IT WAS FOUND THAT THE HEATED DEICE LIP WAS CRACKED AROUND THE SUPPLY DUCT WHERE THE ENGINE EXHAUST ENTERS THE BACK OF THE DEICE LIP.  THIS ALLOWED EXHAUST GASES TO ESCAPE INSIDE THE COWLING AND TO BE DRAWN DOWN THE ENGINE INLET CREATING A DEFINED STREAK IN THE INLET.  THIS FAILURE HAS BEEN FOUND IN SEVERAL OTHER OF OUR FLEET OF AIRCRAFT.  THE PILATUS APPROVED REPAIR, UNDER PILATUS SERVICE BULLETIN 71-003, WAS TO INSTALL AN UPGRADED DEICE LIP TO PC-12 MSN 181-260.  THIS PARTICULAR SERVICE BULLETIN WAS INCORPORATED AT THE FACTORY ON MSN 261 AND SUBSEQUENT.  PER SB 71-003 THE LIP WAS REPLACED TO PREVENT SMALL CRACKS FROM PROPAGATING ON THE BACK SIDE OF THE LIP ASSY.  OUR ENTIRE FLEET OF PC-12 AIRCRAFT HAVE BEEN UPGRADED TO THE NEW STYLE DEICE INLET LIP, P/N 530.24.12.151, OR P/N 530.24.12.155.  THIS REPAIR HAS NOT PREVENTED THE DEICE LIP FROM CRACKING ON THE AFT SIDE OF THE DEICE LIP ASSEMBLY.  ALSO, THE FREQUENCY OF FAILURE HAS REMAINED CONSISTENT AROUND 1400-4000 HOURS OF OPERATION BEFORE FAILURE.

THE ENGINE WAS SHUT DOWN SHORTLY AFTER LANDING AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS TAXIED SAFELY TO THE FBO. ATI JET MAINTENANCE WAS SENT TO  INVESTIGATE THE ISSUE. AN OIL SEAL ON THE PRIMARY MAGNETIC ALTERNATOR (PMA) WAS WORN AND SLIGHTLY TORN CAUSING THE LEAK. A NEW SEAL WAS INSTALLED AND THE OIL RESERVOIR SERVICED TO FULL. THE ENGINE WAS RUN UP  TO FULL POWER, NO LEAKS NOTED. THE AIRCRAFT WAS  RETURNED TO SERVICE AND HAS MADE TWO TRIPS WITH NO ISSUES OR LEAKS REPORTED.

ON SATURDAY, JANUARY 6, CAPTAIN EXPERIENCED A SERVICE DIFFICULTY IN OUR N402PA (CESSNA 402-B)  AIRCRAFT ON A PART 135 FLIGHT.  CAPTAIN WAS UNABLE TO MOVE THE RIGHT FUEL SELECTOR FROM THE "AUX" TO THE "MAIN" POSITION. AS A RESULT, THE RIGHT ENGINE EXPERIENCED FUEL STARVATION AND FLAMED OUT ON FINAL TO FXE AIRPORT.  CAPTAIN ADVISED FXE TOWER OF THE SITUATION. HE DID NOT DECLARE AN EMERGENCY SINCE THE AIRCRAFT WAS STABILIZED AND PERFORMED ACCORDINGLY. OUR GENERAL OPERATIONS MANUAL GIVES THE PIC FINAL AUTHORITY OF THE FLIGHT; IT DOES NOT SPECIFY ANY EVENT THAT REQUIRES A MANDATORY DECLARATION OF EMERGENCY.  THE FLIGHT ENDED IN AN UNEVENTFUL SINGLE-ENGINE LANDING AND TAXI TO CUSTOMS AT FXE.
UPON TAXI FROM CUSTOMS TO THE HANGAR, THE RIGHT FUEL SELECTOR BECAME OPERABLE AGAIN.  CAPTAIN DID NOT ADD ANY FUEL AFTER LANDING AND PARKED THE AIRCRAFT AT AIR FLIGHT'S BASE OF OPERATION.  TO INVESTIGATE THE ISSUE, MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL DRAINED 30 GALLONS OF FUEL FROM EACH MAIN TANK, A SMALL AMOUNT FROM THE LEFT AUX, AND ZERO FUEL FROM THE RIGHT AUX TANK. IT WAS FOUND THAT THE RIGHT FUEL SELECTOR VALVE WAS DEFECTIVE.  CAPTAINS WB SHEET FOR THE FLIGHT FROM MYAK TO FXE SHOWS A TOTAL FUEL LOAD OF 700LBS, CONSISTENT WITH A PRIOR FULL-FUEL TAKEOFF FOR THE REPOSITION FLIGHT FROM FXE TO MYAK.

THE AIRCRAFT HAD LANDED AND AS THE PILOTS BROUGHT THE POWER LEVER INTO BETA/REVERSE, THE LEFT SIDE PILOT DOOR FELL OFF. IT FELL FORWARD OVER THE MLG STRUT. THE DOOR HIT THE GROUND AND WAS THEN RUN OVER BY THE LEFT WHEEL. THE DOOR WAS THEN THROWN BACK UNDER THE FUSELAGE AND HIT THE BELLY. THE LOWER DOOR LOCK PIN PUNCTURED THE BELLY SKIN JUST INBOARD AND FORWARD OF THE CABIN STEP.  THE DOOR THEN FLIPPED OUTBOARD AND AWAY FROM THE AIRCRAFT. THE DOOR WAS BADLY DAMAGED. THE DOOR HANDLE WAS FOUND TO BE IN THE LOCKED POSITION WHEN THE DOOR WAS RECOVERED AND THE DOOR JETTISON HANDLE IN THE CABIN WAS STILL SAFETY WIRED WITH 0.020" BRASS SAFETY WIRE. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION IT WAS FOUND THAT THE DOOR JETTISON HANDLE COULD MOVE ABOUT A ¼" EVEN THOUGH IT WAS SAFETY WIRED. WE THINK THAT THE DOOR DEPARTED THE AIRCRAFT UPON LANDING DUE TO THE DOOR JETTISON HANDLE BEING ABLE TO MOVE SLIGHTLY AND THE FORCES ON THE AIRCRAFT DURING LANDING. THE LANDING WAS RECORDED AS BEING 1.3 G’S BY THE EI MVP-50T (RECORDING 3 LINES PER SECOND). THE DOORS WERE CHECKED FOR VERTICAL PLAY PER THE PILATUS AMM SEC 52-10-00 AT THE LAST INSPECTION (WITHIN LIMITS). THE AMM ALSO CALLS FOR .5 MM BRASS LOCKWIRE TO SECURE THE JETTISON HANDLE WITH NO METHOD SPECIFIED.  WE FOUND THAT IF A SINGLE LOOP OF WIRE WAS USED THE LOCKWIRE WOULD UNRAVEL AS THE HANDLE WAS PULLED. BETWEEN INSPECTIONS THE JETTISON HANDLE CAN BECOME LOOSE. WE THINK 3 LOOPS OF BRASS LOCKWIRE ARE NEEDED TO BETTER SECURE THE HANDLE.

EXPERIENCED A SMOKE IN THE COCKPIT EVENT DURING 133 FLIGHT. TAKEOFF WAS AT 10:22AM IN VFR CONDITIONS. BEFORE BEGINNING THE APPROACH TO THE SHIP, I PUT THE GEAR DOWN AND SWITCHED ON HOIST POWER. AS WE NEARED THE HOISTING LOCATION AT THE BRIDGE WING AT APPROXIMATELY 10:31, I COMMENTED TO THE HOIST OPERATOR THAT I COULD SMELL THE STACK GAS FROM THE EXHAUST OF THE VESSEL. HE REPLIED THAT IT SMELLED LIKE ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT BURNING. I BROUGHT MY EYES BACK INSIDE THE COCKPIT AND SAW SMOKE BILLOWING FROM THE HOIST POWER PANEL IN THE CENTER CONSOLE. I IMMEDIATELY SWITCHED IT OFF, CALLED IT OUT AND ABORTED THE APPROACH. AS I TRANSITIONED TO FORWARD FLIGHT, BOTH PFD’S AND MFD’S WENT BLACK. AFTER ENSURING A STRAIGHT AND LEVEL FLIGHT PATH, I LIFTED MY VISOR AND FOUND THAT THE SCREENS WERE DIMMED TO THE LOWEST SETTING AND COULD NOT BE ADJUSTED. I CONFIRMED THE AUTOPILOT WAS ENGAGED THEN ASKED THE HOIST OPERATOR TO RUN THROUGH THE “SMOKE IN THE COCKPIT” EMERGENCY PROCEDURE FROM THE QRH. THE SMOKE HAD REDUCED CONSIDERABLY AND WE WERE FORCED TO FLY BACK WITH THE DOOR OPEN AT 75 KNOTS BECAUSE THERE WAS SERVAL FEET OF CABLE OUT. WE LANDED AT 10:44 AND THE MECHANICS BEGAN THEIR INSPECTION. AT THIS TIME THE FAILURE SEEMS TO HAVE BEEN ISOLATED TO THE HOIST POWER PANEL WHICH IS A SEALED COMPONENT. THERE’S NO EXTERNAL EVIDENCE OF ARCING OR BURNING ON THE CASE OR CONNECTOR.

AIRCRAFT DEPARTED KSHR AT 1840Z FOR A MAINTENANCE FLIGHT.  DURING CLIMB OUT THE PILOT ASKED THE COPILOT TO MOVE THE TEMPERATURE CONTROL HANDLE FOR HEAT.  THE COPILOT OPENED THE HEAT VALVE WITH THE TEMPERATURE CONTROL HANDLE AND EXPERIENCED A SLIGHT "POP".  THE HEAT REMAINED IN THE OPEN POSITION FOR A BRIEF TIME UNTIL THE CREW HAD SMOKE IN THE CABIN AND COCKPIT.  THE COPILOT ATTEMPTED TO SECURE THE TEMPERATURE CONTROL HANDLE, BUT COULD NOT RETURN THE HANDLE TO THE OFF POSITION DUE TO BINDING.  THE CREW IMMEDIATELY RETURNED TO KSH WHERE THE AIRCRAFT WAS INSPECTED FOR THE CAUSE OF THE BINDING AND SMOKE.  DURING THE INVESTIGATION IT WAS NOTED THE RIGHT ENGINE BLEED VALVE LINKAGE WAS SLIGHTLY MISADJUSTED CAUSING THE VALVE LEVER AND LINKAGE TO BIND IN AN OVER-CENTER POSITION RESULTING IN THE BLEED VALVES STAYING OPEN.  THIS RESULTED IN DAMAGE TO THE INTERIOR INSULATION BLANKETS INSTALLED NEXT TO THE HEATING DUCT AND THIS IS BELIEVED TO BE THE SOURCE OF THE SMOKE.  THE LINKAGE WAS ADJUSTED AND AIRCRAFT HEATING SYSTEM WAS OPERATED DURING A GROUND RUN WITH NO FURTHER ADVERSE EFFECTS.

THE SCREW JACK ID PLATE SHOWS THE PART NUMBER TO BE FE151-007, IF SB17 HAS BEEN PERFORMED, AS STATED ON THE PREVIOUS 8130-3  SERVICE BULLETIN 47145-27-08 IS A CONCURRENT REQUIREMENT AND SHOULD HAVE BEEN COMPLETED AS WELL. ACCOMPLISHING 47145-27-08 WILL CHANGE THE PN OF THE SCREW JACK TO FE151-011 AS WELL AS THE PN OF THE THSA TO A 47145-X4X. DUE TO THE PREVIOUS REPAIR HISTORY PROVIDED BY ALLEGIANT, IT WAS THOUGHT THAT THE SCREW JACK OR THE THSA COULD BE INCORRECTLY IDENTIFIED. TO CONFIRM, THE SCREW JACK ASSEMBLY WAS DISASSEMBLED TO THRUST BEARING MATERIAL WAS INSPECTED TO DETERMINE IF THE SB 47145-27-08 WAS ACCOMPLISHED. THE TECHNICIAN WAS ABLE TO CONFIRM THE SB WAS ACCOMPLISHED; HOWEVER, THEY NOTED VISIBLE SIGNS OF DAMAGE ON THE DOWEL PINS WHICH WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN FOUND IT THE DATA PLATE FOR THE SCREW JACK ASSEMBLY AND THE THSA WERE IDENTICAL.   REASON FOR CONCERN: POTENTIAL HIDDEN DAMAGE. THESE PINS SIT IN PREDRILLED HOLES THAT LINE UP PERFECTLY WHEN THE NO-BACK NUT IS TORQUED DOWN ON THE NO-BACK HOUSING WITH A SHIM IN-BETWEEN. IF ONE OF THESE THREE PARTS ARE NOT LINED UP, NOT ALL THE PINS CAN BE INSERTED FULLY. THIS PIN POTENTIALLY COULD HAVE BEEN USED TO LINE EVERYTHING UP WHEN TORQUING THE NUT DOWN AND BACKING IT OFF CONTINUOUSLY UNTIL THE PIN FELL INTO PLACE ALIGNING THE NUT, SHIM AND HOUSING.

ON 3/30/2024, DEPARTED KMBS WITH PASSENGERS HEADING TO KSAT. ABOUT 20 MINS INTO FLT, CREW NOTICED A FUEL IMBALANCE IN WINGS. ON CHECKING FUEL CONTROL SWITCH PANEL, NOTICED RT STANDBY PUMP ILLUMINATED & RT JET PUMP WAS TURNED OFF. CAPTAIN CALLED MAINT WHEN ISSUE FIRST NOTICED. DETERMINED TO LAND.  CREW LANDED IN KSBN.  TAXIED TO PARKING, CAPTAIN VERIFIED LIGHTS WERE ON. SHUT ACFT DOWN. CREW WENT BACK TO ACFT TO TROUBLESHOOT ISSUE. WHEN POWER WAS APPLIED TO ACFT, LIGHTS WERE OUT. POWER CYCLED SEVERAL TIMES TO DUPLICATE ISSUE, DETERMINED LIGHTS HAD COME ON DURING START SEQUENCE WHICH STANDBY PUMP ON & JET PUMP OFF IS NORMAL & CAME BACK ON AT SOME POINT DURING FLT. SEVERAL START ATTEMPTS MADE TO CHECK VALVE SEQUENCING. ALL STARTS NORMAL,  ISSUE COULD NOT BE DUPLICATED. OPS & MAINT DECIDED TO HAVE THE CREW FLY TO MAINT HOMEBASE TO LOOK INTO THE ISSUER. SHORT FLIGHTS TO KICT THEN KELP WERE PLANNED. ACFT COMPLETED THE FLIGHTS INTO KELP & LANDED SAFELY WITH NO OTHER ISSUES. START SEQUENCE PROCESS WAS VERIFIED & ISSUE WAS DUPLICATED.  SPEED SENSOR CONNECTOR ON RT STARTER WAS FOUND TO BE CAUSING THE ISSUE, START SEQUENCE DID NOT REVERSE/DISENGAGE STANDBY PUMP & JET PUMP AFTER STARTER REACHED A CERTAIN RPM.  CONNECTOR FOUND SECURED & SAFETY WIRED BUT THE LOCKING COLLAR WAS WOBBLY & NOT TIGHT. WHILE THE ENGINE WAS RUNNING, MAINTENANCE HAD A HAND ON THE CONNECTOR, AND WHILE MOVING THE CONNECTOR, THE PUMP LIGHTS CAME BACK ON AND WENT OUT WHEN HELD TIGHT. NEW CONNECTOR AND BACK SHELL ORDERED.

AN OIL LEAK WAS FOUND ON THE ENGINE LUBRICATION UNIT WHERE THE AFT SUMP OIL SCAVENGE TUBE CONNECTS TO THE LUBRICATION UNIT.  THE OIL SCAVENGE TUBE WAS REMOVED AND A NEW GASKET WAS INSTALLED.  THE FOUR ATTACHING BOLTS WERE INSTALLED AND TORQUED PER THE AMM, USING A CALIBRATED TORQUE WRENCH.  THE ENGINE RUN WAS ACCOMPLISHED WITH NO OIL LEAKS NOTED.  A FLIGHT WAS INITIATED AND WHILE IN FLIGHT THE SCAVENGE OIL LINE LEAKED AT THE LUBRICATION UNIT, REQUIRING AN INFLIGHT SHUTDOWN OF THE ENGINE.  MAINTENANCE REMOVED THE OIL LINE FROM THE LUBRICATION UNIT.  INSPECTION FOUND THE THREADED INSERTS IN THE FOUR ATTACHING HOLES OF THE LUBRICATION UNIT HAD BACKED OUT AND WERE PROTRUDING ABOVE THE SURFACE OF THE LUBRICATION UNIT.  THIS CONDITION PREVENTED THE GASKET FROM SEALING BETWEEN THE UNIT AND OIL LINE.  THE LUBRICATION UNIT WAS SUBSEQUENTLY REPLACED WITH NO FURTHER LEAKS.  THE THREADED INSERTS IN THE LUBRICATION UNIT SHOULD BE INSPECTED TO MAKE SURE THEY ARE SECURE, INSTALLED CORRECTLY AND NOT PROTRUDING ABOVE THE MATING SURFACE WHEN OIL LINES ARE ATTACHED TO THE LUBRICATION UNIT.

AIRCRAFT CRASHED DURING AN ATTEMPTED OFF-AIRPORT LANDING NEAR ALPINE, ARKANSAS. THE PILOT WAS UNINJURED BUT THE AIRCRAFT SUSTAINED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE. THE PILOT EXPERIENCED SYMPTOMS OF CARBON MONOXIDE POISONING AND BOTH CARBON MONOXIDE (CO) DETECTORS ALERTED.  FAA AND NTSB CONDUCTED INSPECTION OF EXHAUST AND CABIN AIR VENTILATION SYSTEM. THE SCAT AIR DUCT THAT SUPPLIED HEATED AIR TO THE CABIN VENTILATION SYSTEM WAS COMPROMISED IN TWO AREAS IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT TO THIS UNAPPROVED WELD. THE CABIN VENTILATION AIR BOX LOCATED ON THE FIREWALL REVEALED THE MANUALLY OPERATED VALVE WHICH CONTROLS THE SUPPLY OF HEATED AIR TO THE COCKPIT WAS COMPLETELY DETACHED FROM ITS ACTUATING ARM. WITH THIS BREAK, THE PILOT HAD NO CONTROL OF THE CABIN HEAT. A CLOSER INSPECTION OF THE BREAK REVEALED SIGNIFICANT CORROSION INDICATIVE OF A LONG-PREEXISTING BREAK. BASED ON THE INSPECTION, THE FAULTY AND UNAPPROVED EXHAUST WELD ALLOWED HIGH-PRESSURE SUPER-HEATED EXHAUST GAS TO CONCENTRATE ON ONE AREA OF THE SCAT DUCT WHICH EVENTUALLY BURNT A HOLE IN THE DUCT ALLOWING CO GAS TO INFILTRATE THE CABIN AIR SYSTEM. A FAULTY CABIN AIR VALVE GAVE THE CO FREE AND UNOBSTRUCTED ACCESS INTO THE COCKPIT. THIS GAS INFILTRATION WAS RECOGNIZED BY THE CO ALARMS. THE DIRECT CAUSE OF THE HIGH CARBON MONOXIDE LEVEL WAS THIS FAULTY CABIN AIR VALVE. IF THE VALVE WERE OPERATING AS DESIGNED, THE PILOT WOULD HAVE STOPPED THE CARBON MONOXIDE INFILTRATION BY MANUALLY SHUTTING THE CABIN HEAT VALVE.

A FAULTY CABIN AIR VALVE REMOVED THE PILOT'S ABILITY TO ISOLATE THE CABIN FROM THE EXHAUST GASES AND THE BUILDUP OF CARBON MONOXIDE CAUSED THE SENSORS TO ALERT.

AFTER DISCUSSING THE ISSUE WITH OPERATIONS, THE DECISION WAS MADE TO RUN THE ENGINES TO DIAGNOSE THE ISSUE AND IF ALL WAS CLEAR, REPOSITION THE AIRCRAFT TO KELP FOR MAINTENANCE. THE ENGINE RUNS WERE COMPLETED WITH VERY MINOR REMNANTS OF THE SMELL. THE CREW DECIDED TO CONTINUE WITH THE REPOSITION TO KELP. CLIMBING OUT OF TEB IN THE MID 30S THE AIRCRAFT WAS UNABLE TO MAINTAIN ADDITIONAL CABIN PRESSURE. THE CREW LEVELED OFF AND ASSESSED THE SITUATION, AND AFTER SOME TROUBLE SHOOTING ELECTED THAT THE FLIGHT WAS UNABLE TO CONTINUE TO AUSTIN AT THAT POINT IN TIME.

FROM KSAT TO MYNN WHEN WE EXPERIENCED AN ENGINE FAILURE IN FLIGHT.  AT FLIGHT LEVEL 390 APPROXIMATELY 100 MILES WEST OF THE SOUTHERN COAST OF FLORIDA, THE LEFT (#1) ENGINE ROLLED BACK QUITE ABRUPTLY IN FLIGHT.  WE DECLARED AN EMERGENCY DUE TO THE LOSS OF THRUST AND THE CABIN PRESSURE RISING SINCE ONLY 1 ENGINE WAS SUPPLYING PRESSURIZATION.  UPON OUR DECENT DOWN TO 10,000 FEET, WE COMMENCED OUR SOPS AND RUN THROUGH OUR EMERGENCY CHECKLIST.  THE FIRST ONE CALLS TO SECURE THE ENGINE AND TAKE IT OFFLINE.  AFTER COMPLETING THIS WE ARE TO MAKE THE DECISION TO TRY AND RESTART IT.  BECAUSE THERE WAS NO INDICATION OF FIRE, FOREIGN OBJECT DEBRIS, OR FROZEN FAN (N1 OR N2), WE DECIDED TO RESTART THE ENGINE.  AFTER RUNNING THROUGH THE PROPER CHECKLIST TO RESTART THE ENGINE, WE COULD NOT GET THE ENGINE TO LIGHT OFF.   SO, WE DECIDED TO RESECURE THE ENGINE AND CONTINUE TO ON TO OUR DIVERSION AIRPORT, KRSW, WITH ONE ENGINE AND LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.  WE CONTINUED WITH THE "SINGLE ENGINE APPROACH TO LANDING" CHECKLIST AND LANDED THE PLANE AT KRSW.  THIS IS A 12,000FT RUNWAY AND AFTER RUNNING THE LANDING DISTANCE WITH PARTIAL FLAPS WE CONCLUDED IT WAS MORE THAN LONG ENOUGH.  THE LANDING ITSELF TURNED OUT TO BE A NON-EVENT AND WE WERE ABLE TO SAFELY TAXI TO THE FBO AND SAFELY DE-PLANE THE PASSENGERS.

CREW CONTACTED JET OUT'S MAINTENANCE DEPARTMENT, IT WAS THEN DETERMINED TO RESTART THE ENGINE. CREW RAN THE ENGINE WHILE IN CONTACT WITH THE MAINTENANCE DEPARTMENT. AFTER COMPLETION OF THE GROUND RUNS/CHECKS IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE ENGINE/AIRCRAFT WAS OKAY FOR THE FLIGHT TO HOME BASE. DOWNLOADS FROM THE ONBOARD MONITORING SYSTEM (ARES) WERE SENT TO TEXTRON AVIATION FOR REVIEW. THE DOWNLOADS SHOWED THE FLIGHT CREW HAD DEPRESSED THE SWITCH STARTING THE ENGINE, AND DURING THE TAKEOFF ROLL THIS SWITCH APPEARED TO DISENGAGED. DURING FURTHER INVESTIGATION WITH WILLIAMS INTERNATIONAL (ENGINE MANUFACTURE) AND TEXTRON AVIATION (AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURE) WE WERE INFORMED THAT TEXTRON AVIATION IS AWARE OF THE ISSUE. THEY STATED IF THE FLIGHT CREW DOES NOT FULLY DEPRESS THE "RUN/STOP" SWITCH WHEN STARTING THE ENGINE, THE ENGINE WILL START BUT AT SOME POINT DURING AIRCRAFT OPERATION THE SWITCH MAY DISENGAGE, CAUSING THE ASSOCIATED ENGINE TO SHUT DOWN. ALSO, THEY NOTED THAT THE SWITCH MY HANG UP WHEN DEPRESSED, AT THEN DISENGAGE AT A LATER TIME DUE TO VIBRATION FOR EXAMPLE. JET OUT LLC HAS ADDED ADDITIONAL TRAINING TO OUR FLIGHT CREWS TO ADDRESS THIS SITUATION.

MTU RECOGNIZED THAT CERTAIN OVERTEMPERATURE INSPECTIONS WERE NOT PERFORMED ON ESN 690328 IN THE PAST. THIS WAS NOTICED BECAUSE THE WORKSCOPE OF ESN 690328 WAS USED AS A REFERENCE DURING WORKSCOPE PREPARATION FOR ANOTHER ENGINE WHICH SUFFERED EGT OVERTEMPERATURE. THE OVERTEMPERATURE OF ESN 690328 OCCURRED TWICE DURING OUTGOING TESTRUN (MTU PROJECT NUMBER L.10872) N AUG. 2020 (START #10 FOR 10 SECONDS > 1600°F WITH A MAXIMUM OF 1778°F AND DURING START #12 FOR 10 SECONDS > 1600°F WITH MAXIMUM OF 1770°F). WITH OEM CASE #01288488 GE WAS ASKED TO WAIVE ALL OVERTEMPERATURE INSPECTIONS FOR THIS ENGINE.   GE ANSWERED THAT “IT IS REQUIRED TO DO AN INSPECTION/CHECK FOR OVERTEMPERATURE OPERATION. REFER TO TASK 72-00-00-200-828 (PARAGRAPH 3.) AS ENGINE EGT OVERTEMPERATURE CONDITION DID OCCUR TWICE (DURING START 10: 1778°F AND DURING START 12: 1770°F), GE RECOMMENDS TO PERFORM ABOVE REFERENCED INSPECTION/CHECK FOR OVERTEMPERATURE OPERATION.”
BASED ON THE ANSWER THE ENGINE WAS REINDUCTED UNDER MTU-PROJECT-NUMBER V.00535 TO PERFORM THE OVERTEMPERATURE INSPECTION TASKS WITHIN THE SHOP VISIT.
BUT THE GE INSTRUCTIONS WERE MISINTERPRETED BECAUSE “(PARAGRAPH 3.)” - MEANING PARAGRAPH 3. G. (1) TO (6) - WAS UNDERSTOOD AS “(3)” OF TASK 72-00-00-200-828 ONLY, WHICH REFLECTS ONLY HPT ROTOR ASSEMBLY OVERTEMPERATURE INSPECTIONS (REFER TO FIGURE 1). THEREFORE, SEVERAL OVERTEMPERATURE INSPECTIONS WERE NOT PERFORMED IN 2020 (UNDER MTU-PROJECT- NUMBER V.00535), REFER TO TABLE 1. THE ENGINE WAS DELIVERED TO THE CUSTOMER AND OPERATED FOR 2.202 CYCLES AND 6.280 HOURS UNTIL NEXT SHOPVISIT IN 2023/2024. THE CUSTOMER DID NOT REPORT ANY UNUSUAL FINDING OR EVENT DURING OPERATION.
ESN 690328 WAS AT MTU H FOR ANOTHER SHOP VISIT IN IN 2023/24 WHICH WAS HANDELED UNDER MTU-PROJECT-NUMBERS L.15619 AND L.16315 AND WAS A PERFORMANCE RESTORATION. THUS, SOME OF THE OPEN INSPECTIONS WERE PERFORMED DURING THIS SHOPVISIT ALTHOUGH MTU WAS NOT AWARE THAT THEY WERE NOT PERFORMED DURING THE LAST SHOPVISIT. NEVERTHELESS OVERTEMPERATURE INSPECTIONS FOR SEVERAL PARTS ARE STILL NOT PERFORMED IN FULL. DURING THE PERFORMED INSPECTIONS THERE WERE NO UNUSUAL FINDINGS PER INCOMING INSPECTION REPORT.
THE ENGINE WAS DELIVERED TO THE CUSTOMER AND IS NOW IN OPERATION. THE ENGINE CONDITION MONITORING FOR ESN 690328 IS CONTRACTED TO MTU. UNTIL TODAY THE ENGINE HAS ACCOMPLISHED 248 CYCLES SINCE LAST SHOPVISIT.
UNTIL TODAY THE CUSTOMER DID NOT REPORT ANY UNUSUAL FINDING OR EVENT DURING OPERATION.

NOW FULLY OUT OF THE WATER WE SKIDDED SIDEWAYS FOR 5 FT. THIS ACTION BENT THE SPREADER BARS AND ROLLED THE RIGHT FLOAT UNDER. TOWARDS THE END OF A PATIENT TRANSPORT LEG - ABOUT 2 MINUTES OUT FROM LANDING AT ROOFTOP HOSPITAL HELIPAD.  EXPERIENCED MASTER CAUTION LIGHT IN CONJUNCTION WITH MULTIPLE CAUTION LIGHTS ON THE NUMBER 2 ENGINE SIDE AND CENTER LANE OF CAD. COINCIDENTLY WITH THESE ENUNCIATIONS I AND MY MEDICAL CREW STATED THAT WE SMELLED SMOKE. WERE ABOUT 3 MILES FROM OUR INTENDED LANDING PAD AND ABOUT 2.5 MILES SOUTH OF ALBANY INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KALB).  BEGAN TO SLOW AND ESTABLISH OEI FLIGHT CONDITIONS AND TURN TOWARDS THE AIRPORT. I DID NOT SEE A FIRE INDICATION, AND WAS FOCUSED ON THE LOSS OF MY NUMBER 2 N2 AND ROTOR INDICATION ON THE TRIPLE TACH. AT THIS TIME I DETERMINED THE NR 2 ENGINE WAS FAILED. AT THIS POINT, I VERY CAUTIOUSLY LOCATED MY ENGINE 2 THROTTLE AND PROCEEDED TO SLOWLY ROLL IT OFF TO SECURE IT. WHILE DOING THIS I REMAINED FOCUSED ON THE NUMBER 1 ENGINE TO MAKE SURE I WAS SECURING THE CORRECT ENGINE. WHILE CONTINUING TO SLOW AND FLY TOWARDS THE AIRPORT I ATTEMPTED TO DECLARE EMERGENCY ON THE APPROACH FREQUENCY THAT I WAS ON WITH THE NUMBER 2 RADIO. AT THIS POINT I DISCOVERED I HAD NO ELECTRICAL POWER TO THAT RADIO AND TRANSPONDER; POWER WAS STILL SUPPLIED TO THE NUMBER 1 RADIO WHICH I TUNED TO THAT FREQUENCY AND ATTEMPTED TO CALL ON THAT RADIO. THIS TRANSMISSION WAS UNSUCCESSFUL BECAUSE I NOTICED THERE WAS NO POWER TO THE RADIO CONTROL HEADS. COULD HEAR ATC ATTEMPT TO CONTACT ME ASKING ME TO IDENT WHICH I TRIED AND COULD NOT ACCOMPLISH DUE TO THERE BEING NO POWER TO TRANSPONDER. I THEN ASKED THE MEDICAL CREW IF ANY OF THEM COULD COMMUNICATE WITH ATC. THE MEDIC STATED HE HAD POWER ON HIS CONTROL HEAD, I ASKED HIM TO RELAY OUR EMERGENCY TO ATC WHICH HE WAS ABLE TO DO. I COULD HEAR ATC CLEAR US FOR ANY AND ALL RUNWAYS. AS I CONTINUED WITH THE SHALLOW SINGLE ENGINE APPROACH (STILL 1.5 MINUTES OUT) I ACTIVATED THE NR 2 ENGINE EMERGENCY CUTOFF, WHICH ENUNCIATED ACTIVE. I THEN COMPLETED THE RUN ON LANDING ON RUNWAY 01 WITHOUT FURTHER INCIDENT. AFTER LANDING, COMPLETED SHUTDOWN OF ALL REMAINING SYSTEMS PER THE CHECKLIST.

THE PRESSURE WAS SLIGHTLY ABOVE ZERO AS THE WERE LINING UP FOR LANDING. THE CAPTAIN DECIDED TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY. THE AIRCRAFT WAS LANDED SAFELY AND TAXIED BACK TO THE FBO. ALL FUNCTIONS REQUIRING HYDRAULIC PRESSURE WERE COMPLETED BY RESIDUAL PRESSURE FROM ENGINES AND THE STAND BY HYDRAULIC PUMP. NO EMERGENCY AIR WAS NEEDED FOR GEAR EXTENSION OR AIRCRAFT BRAKING. ATI JET MAINTENANCE WAS DISPATCHED TO KLBB WITH PARTS AND SUPPLIES. THE DEFECTIVE HOSE WAS REPLACED, THE HYDRAULIC FILTERS WERE REMOVED, FLUSHED AND INSPECTED FOR CONTAMINATION. NO CONTAMINATION FOUND IN THE PRESSURE OR RETURN FILTERS. NEW FILTERS WERE INSTALLED AND THE HYDRAULIC RESERVOIR WAS SERVICED. THE STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP WAS RUN AND REQUIRED BLEEDING, A SMALL AMOUNT OF AIR WAS RELEASED DURING THE PROCESS. THE ENGINES WERE RUN INDIVIDUALLY AND PRESSURE INDICATION WAS NORMAL ON BOTH. AFTER TOPPING OFF THE RESERVOIR, THE CREW DECIDED IT WAS SAFE TO ATTEMPT THE RETURN FLIGHT TO KELP. THE FLIGHT WAS COMPLETED WITH NOT ISSUES/DISCREPANCIES REPORTED.

THE HUMAN FACTOR IS ALSO SUSPECTED, FURTHER INVESTIGATIONS ARE ON-GOING.  CONTAINMENT ACTIONS ARE DONE AND CORRECTIVES ACTION HAVE BEEN ENGAGED WITH MODIFICATION OF THE SAID CHECK-LISTS AND JOB CARD. A STUDY IS ALSO LAUNCHED FOR ADDING A VISUAL TEMPORARY MARKING AT REMOVAL TO HELP INSTALLATION BACK OF THE FLEX HOSE.  ROOT CAUSES ARE ALL IDENTIFIED AND AS THE ASSOCIATED CONTAINEMENT/CORRECTIVES ACTIONS ARE COMPLETED (SEE ATTACHED) SAE PROPOSE THE CLOSURE OF THIS OCCURRENCE REPORT.

WE HAD JUST LEVELED OFF AT 14,000' FOR CRUISE WHEN THE MED CREW REPORTED SMOKE AND THE SMELL OF SOMETHING BURNING IN THE CABIN.  I LOOKED AND THERE WASN'T MUCH SMOKE, BUT IT WAS THERE. I COULD BARELY SMELL IT IN THE COCKPIT BUT IT APPEARED TO BE THICKER IN THE CABIN.  THEY SAID IT KIND OF SMELLED LIKE A CROSS BETWEEN ELECTRICAL AND OVERHEATING HEATER. THEY WERE UNABLE TO LOCATE WHERE IT WAS COMING FROM. I TURNED THE HEAT ALL THE WAY DOWN AND THE SMOKE SEEMED TO DISSIPATE AFTER A FEW MINUTES. WE WERE OVER HALFWAY AT THAT POINT SO WE ELECTED TO CONTINUE ON TO KWRL. CORRECTIVE ACTION: WITH THE CABIN TEMP MODE AND VENT BLOWER IN “AUTO”, ELECTRIC GROUND HEAT IN “NORMAL”, AND THE CABIN TEMP SET TO “HIGH”, AND THE COCKPIT VENTS CLOSED AND CABIN AIR SET TO FULL DECREASE, EXCESSIVE HEAT AND MINIMAL AIR FLOW WAS FOUND AT THE REGISTERS.  THIS CONFIGURATION MATCHED THE CONFIGURATION OF THE FLIGHT THAT PRODUCED A BURNING SMELL AND SMOKE.  IN THIS CONFIGURATION ON THE GROUND, THE SMELL OF HOT PLASTIC WAS APPARENT, BUT THE CONFIGURATION WAS CHANGED BEFORE ANY SMOKE WAS PRODUCED.  THE LIGHT SMOKE PRODUCED DURING FLIGHT WAS LIKELY THE RESULT OF  FUZZ, LINT, AND OR DUST BUILT UP IN THE DUCTS, VALVES, AND PLENUM BEING EXPOSED TO THE HIGH HEAT OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL PLUMBING. INCREASING CABIN AIR AND OPENING COCKPIT VENTS IMMEDIATELY CAUSED THE TEMPERATURES AT THE REGISTERS TO DECREASE AND DISSIPATED THE HOT PLASTIC SMELL.  THE CAUSE OF THE DISCREPANCY WAS FOUND TO BE CALLING FOR HIGH HEAT WITH ALL COCKPIT VENTS CLOSED AND CABIN AIR SET TO FULL DECREASE. NO DEFECTS FOUND AT THIS TIME.

THE CANOPY LATCH ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE FUSELAGE HAS A KEYHOLE NEXT TO THE HANDLE USED TO LOCK THE LATCH HANDLE CLOSED. TO UNLOCK THE CANOPY, YOU INSERT THE KEY INTO THE LOCK CYLINDER AND ROTATE IT 180 DEGREES. YOU THEN ROTATE THE LATCH HANDLE FORWARD TO UNLATCH THE CANOPY.  THE ISSUE ARISES WHEN THE LOCK CYLINDER IS INADVERTENTLY ROTATED AS THE KEY IS BEING REMOVED. THIS ACTION PARTIALLY LOCKS THE LATCH HANDLE, PREVENTING IT FROM FULLY ROTATING BACK INTO THE LOCKED POSITION. AS A RESULT, YOU CAN ENTER THE COCKPIT, CLOSE THE CANOPY, AND ROTATE THE LATCH HANDLE TO WHAT APPEARS TO BE THE LATCHED POSITION. HOWEVER, THE LATCH IS NOT FULLY ENGAGED.  THE MULTIFUNCTION DISPLAY (MFD) COMPOUNDS THE PROBLEM BY PROVIDING A FALSE INDICATION THAT THE CANOPY IS LATCHED BASED SOLELY ON THE POSITION OF THE LOCK CYLINDER, NOT THE ACTUAL ENGAGEMENT OF THE LATCH HANDLE. THIS FALSE INDICATION LEADS THE PILOT TO BELIEVE THE CANOPY IS SECURED WHEN IT IS NOT.  DURING TAKEOFF ROTATION, THE CANOPY CAN POP OPEN DUE TO AERODYNAMIC FORCES. ONCE THE AIRCRAFT IS AIRBORNE, THE CANOPY CANNOT BE RE-SECURED WITHOUT EXTERNAL ACCESS TO THE LOCK CYLINDER. IF THE CANOPY DETACHES MID-FLIGHT, IT COULD POTENTIALLY STRIKE THE EMPENNAGE, CAUSING DAMAGE TO CRITICAL FLIGHT SURFACES AND CREATING A SERIOUS SAFETY HAZARD.
